label: Premise
title: One response. Different token roles.
narration: Preference optimization usually asks one objective to supervise an entire answer. TFPO starts from a different premise: different tokens play different roles, so they should not all receive the same training signal.

label: The conflict
title: Uniform pressure creates interference.
narration: Reasoning tokens determine whether an explanation is helpful and well justified. Final answers, option letters, schema keys, and code fragments often need likelihood anchoring to remain stable and parseable. Applying one sequence-level preference signal everywhere can make these roles interfere.

label: Method
title: Learn where each objective should act.
narration: TFPO adds a lightweight gate to every response token. Low gate values send more weight to a DPO-style preference objective. High values emphasize chosen-response likelihood. In effect, reasoning-sensitive spans receive preference shaping, while answer-bearing spans receive stronger anchoring.

label: Learning the route
title: No token labels are required.
narration: The route is learned from preference pairs, without token labels. Targeted ablations show what each regularizer controls. Removing the ratio penalty raises budget violations from one point six to thirty-six point one percent. Removing total variation increases local switching. Removing entropy raises early saturation from six point four to fifty-two point one percent.

label: Main evaluation
title: A consistent capability gain.
narration: TFPO reaches the highest ten-benchmark average of eighty-eight point zero zero, versus eighty-three point zero eight for SimPO and eighty-three point five two for SimPO plus NLL. Results average three training seeds. BBH, GSM8K, and MATH use fixed two-hundred-prompt subsets with four samples per prompt. Code benchmarks use twenty samples per problem to estimate pass at one.

label: Routing evidence
title: The gate follows content, not position.
narration: The routing claim is tested independently of benchmark accuracy. On one thousand blind annotated responses, the content gate reaches zero point eight five A U P R C, versus zero point five five for the strongest strict position-only control. Moving the answer to the beginning, middle, or end changes TFPO's score by only zero point zero two.

label: Cross-family alignment
title: The gains replicate across backbones.
narration: The same routing recipe is trained independently on Qwen, Llama, and Mistral backbones. TFPO is strongest in every reported AlpacaEval and Arena-Hard column, suggesting that the result is not tied to one tokenizer, instruction-tuning recipe, or model family.

label: Multimodal extension
title: Visual reasoning has fragile conclusions too.
narration: With a Qwen three V L backbone, TFPO reaches the best multimodal average of seventy-one point zero three. The first case illustrates answer formatting, not visual-counting accuracy: TFPO supplies an option letter. The map case illustrates visual grounding. In the numerical case, both TFPO and SimPO reach the correct answer, but TFPO is more concise.

label: Repeated sampling
title: Stable answers, diverse explanations.
narration: Across four matched samples per prompt, TFPO reaches ninety-one point nine seven answer agreement, eighty-six point three three majority accuracy, and ninety point five six average accuracy. Explanation diversity reaches sixty-two point three three. Results average over BBH, GSM8K, and MATH, then three training seeds. Missing or invalid generations remain in the denominator.

label: Takeaway
title: Preference alignment is token-level credit assignment.
narration: TFPO reframes preference optimization as token-level credit assignment between preference shaping and likelihood anchoring. The results show improved performance and answer stability. Strict position controls, blind gold spans, and answer-position counterfactuals provide complementary evidence that the learned route tracks answer-bearing content.
